title: Postmortem Culture
description: Build a blameless postmortem culture that turns production incidents into lasting improvements.

data.text: A postmortem is not a punishment. It is a learning document. When teams adopt blameless postmortems, they stop hiding mistakes and start fixing systems. The result is fewer repeat incidents and stronger trust among teammates.
This lesson shows you how to run effective postmortems, write clear timelines, and convert findings into tracked action items.

Blameless means you ask what happened, not who did it. Humans make mistakes. Systems should be designed to tolerate human error. When people fear blame, they hide details, and teams lose the chance to improve.

items: Focus on process and tooling gaps, not individual actions
Ask what conditions allowed the mistake
Share postmortems openly within the organization

data.title: Pro Tip
data.text: Replace 'Who deployed this?' with 'What checks were missing before deployment?' This simple reframe changes every conversation.

items: Executive Summary: one paragraph on impact and outcome
Timeline: exact times, decisions, and observed symptoms
Root Cause: why the problem started
Contributing Factors: conditions that made it worse
Action Items: specific fixes with owners and due dates
Lessons Learned: generalizable insights for the team

data.text: Root cause is not always a single broken component. Often, multiple conditions combine: a missing alert, a confusing runbook step, and a manual error all contribute. Use the Five Whys or a timeline to find systemic causes.

items: Create a draft within 24 hours of incident resolution
Include timestamps from logs and monitoring tools
Identify at least two action items per postmortem
Assign each action item to a named owner with a due date
Review open action items in the next sprint planning

data.title: Summary
data.text: Postmortem culture is a force multiplier. When teams document incidents openly, patterns emerge, action items get tracked, and systems get stronger. Start small, keep it blameless, and review outcomes regularly.
